q: Is pfaE really at locus tag A7982_13498, or is the paper's identification an unpublished HMMER call that was never propagated into the NCBI GenBank submission?
basis: The paper (Fig. 5AI) asserts pfaE at A7982_13498, but the deposited CP016211.1 GenBank record contains NO CDS whose product string contains 'PPTase', 'phosphopantetheinyl transferase', or 'Sfp'. The replication could not confirm pfaE by keyword, and the paper does not publish the HMM hit table it must have used. This is the largest annotation gap between the paper's Fig. 5 architecture and the underlying deposited record.
next_steps: 1) Run hmmscan (HMMER v3.4) of the full M. rosea proteome against PFAM PF01648 (4'-phosphopantetheinyl transferase); 2) Confirm whether the translation of A7982_13498 scores as a PPTase (bitscore > gathering cutoff); 3) If yes, submit a corrected feature-table update to NCBI adding /product="phosphopantetheinyl transferase"; 4) If no, phylogenetically-place the M. rosea PPTase and publish an errata note. Cost: ~1 CPU-hour, 1 day of agent time.

q: Does the C-terminal AT domain integrated into pfa3 causally explain why M. rosea and Aetherobacter produce DHA/EPA but Sorangium does not, or is the correlation an artifact of comparative-genomics reasoning?
basis: The paper's central mechanistic hypothesis (Discussion of Fig. 5AI vs. AIII) treats integrated-AT as the discriminating molecular feature between DHA/EPA-producing and non-DHA/EPA-producing myxobacterial pfa clusters. This is asserted from comparative genomics alone; no biochemistry (no heterologous expression, no domain-swap experiment, no LC-MS product profiling) is presented. C7 and C8 of the replication also confirm only that the antiSMASH region call is consistent with paper's Fig. 5AI --- not that the AT domain is doing what the paper claims.
next_steps: 1) Heterologously express M. rosea pfa1-pfa3 + pfaE in a fatty-acid-competent Streptomyces coelicolor delta-FAS host (established chassis for prokaryotic PUFA-PKS); 2) Construct a matched delta-AT-domain pfa3 variant by in-frame deletion of the C-terminal AGPAT+AT block; 3) LC-MS profile the total fatty acid pool for DHA (22:6 n-3), EPA (20:5 n-3), ARA (20:4 n-6), and LA (18:2 n-6) with authentic standards; 4) If AT-deletion abolishes DHA/EPA but retains shorter-chain PUFAs, the paper's causal claim is supported; if not, the correlation is spurious and the biosynthetic-mechanism story needs revision. Cost: 3-6 months, wet-lab; ~$40k in reagents+sequencing; requires a collaborator with a Streptomyces PUFA-PKS system (e.g., Zhang lab at ITCR, Salas/Menendez-Bravo at INTECH).

q: Is the paper's 'largest bacterial genome sequenced to date' claim (C11) still true as of 2026?
basis: The claim is time-stamped at 2021 vs. Sorangium cellulosum So0157-2 (14,782,125 bp; 1,258,541 bp smaller than M. rosea's 16,040,666 bp). Neither the paper nor this 2026-07-05 replication has re-surveyed the bacterial genome-size record. Given the 5-year lag, ongoing PacBio HiFi and Nanopore-Q20+ sequencing of large-genome myxobacteria, cyanobacteria (Crocosphaera, Nostoc), and cyanobacterial-bacterial symbionts, the record may have been surpassed. This is not a criticism of the paper but a live open question for the field.
next_steps: 1) Query NCBI datasets CLI for all bacterial (superkingdom Bacteria) assemblies with total_length > 14,000,000 bp deposited between 2021-01-01 and 2026-06-30; 2) Filter to complete or chromosome-level assemblies (exclude scaffold-only); 3) Rank by total_length descending; 4) For any assembly > 16,040,666 bp, verify against original publication; 5) Publish a short update note (JMB/Access Microbiology single-page format) if the record has changed. Cost: 1 agent-day; no wet-lab needed. Deliverable: ranked table + errata-style note.

q: How much of the paper's 'genome-expansion via gene duplication' story survives a modern PacBio HiFi reassembly with duplication-QC?
basis: The paper (44.10% paralogous genes) uses HGAP v2.3.0 (2015-era assembler) and does not report either RepeatMasker/RepeatModeler content nor an assembly-QC pass (Merqury duplication rate, BUSCO duplication metrics). PacBio P6C4 chemistry with 2015-era assemblers is known to inflate apparent paralog counts at repeat boundaries, especially in genomes with >65% GC and heavy secondary-metabolism regions (both true here). The 47-BGC / 1096-gene BGC content of M. rosea is exactly the kind of repetitive-content landscape most prone to assembly-driven paralog inflation. If the paralog rate is significantly lower after HiFi reassembly, the paper's central genome-expansion narrative shifts weight from 'duplication + retention' toward 'HGT + retention'.
next_steps: 1) Pull SRA raw reads for BioProject PRJNA321464 (the paper's PacBio P6C4 dataset); 2) If HiFi CCS data is available, re-assemble with hifiasm-meta or Flye 2.9+; if only CLR is available, re-polish with pbmm2 + gcpp; 3) Run Merqury against a matched short-read k-mer set (if available; else against assembly self-k-mers) to compute duplication rate; 4) Run BUSCO odb10 bacteria_odb10 to independently estimate duplicated single-copy count; 5) Re-classify the paralog set (OrthoFinder or CD-HIT at 30% identity) on the corrected assembly; 6) Compare paralog percentage vs. paper's 44.10%. If drop is >5 percentage points, revisit the paper's genome-expansion mechanism narrative. Cost: ~200 CPU-hours + 1 GPU for assembly; ~1 week agent time.

q: Is the pfa-cluster horizontal-gene-transfer-from-Actinobacteria call (C10) robust to broader taxonomic sampling and to an explicit long-branch-attraction test?
basis: The paper's Fig. 5B trees for Pfa1/Pfa2/Pfa3 include Streptomyces, Azospirillum, Tahibacter, Aetherobacter, Sorangium but do NOT include the broader gamma-proteobacterial PUFA-PKS carriers (Shewanella pneumatophori SCRC-2738, Photobacterium profundum SS9, Moritella marina MP-1) as outgroups, nor a diverse Actinobacterial sweep beyond Streptomyces. The three separate single-gene trees are exactly the topology most vulnerable to long-branch-attraction to the Streptomyces branch --- a well-known failure mode when a fast-evolving lineage is placed near a distant fast-evolving outgroup. The concatenated / model-averaged / AU-test analysis needed to defend HGT rigorously is missing.
next_steps: 1) Assemble a taxon-expanded reference set (n~100): all known myxobacterial pfa clusters + all published gamma-proteobacterial pfa clusters + Actinobacterial homologs across >20 genera (not just Streptomyces) + Azospirillum/Tahibacter + Bacillus PPTase-carrying pfa-like clusters; 2) Individually align Pfa1, Pfa2, Pfa3 with MAFFT-LINSI, trim with trimAl -automated1, concatenate; 3) Run IQ-TREE 2 with ModelFinder + ultrafast bootstrap 1000 + SH-aLRT 1000; 4) Perform an approximately-unbiased (AU) test contrasting (a) paper's Actinobacterial-donor topology vs. (b) vertical inheritance from Sorangiineae ancestor vs. (c) gamma-proteobacterial-donor topology; 5) Run RANGER-DTL v2 with a curated bacterial species tree to explicitly test the HGT-vs-vertical-inheritance likelihood ratio; 6) If AU rejects vertical-inheritance at p<0.01 AND RANGER-DTL prefers HGT-from-Actinobacteria over HGT-from-gamma-proteobacteria, C10 is strengthened. If not, downgrade C10 to speculation and note in an update. Cost: 1-2 weeks compute (~500 CPU-hours) + 1 agent-week analysis; deliverable: publishable methodological note.
